# Kairos

> Kairos is a schedule definition language: a composable time-stream DSL with first-class calendars,
> business days, windows, and projections. Every expression maps a time stream to a time stream
> (closure), so derived dates — substitute holidays, fiscal periods, lunisolar months — can feed
> further definitions. It expresses schedules that cron, Quartz, and iCalendar RRULE cannot, such as
> "3 business days before month-end" or "the first business day on or after February 1".

Key facts:

- Status: 1.0 (declared 2026-09-14). Semantics, operators, grammar (EBNF), and lexis are
  frozen; naming is final for every word (the last placeholder was settled as `rephase`).
- Architecture: two layers — a premise layer that defines calendars (the Gregorian calendar itself is
  a transparent standard library written in Kairos) and a body layer that composes schedules from
  stream-to-stream operators (`roll`, `shift`, `filter`, `nth`, `stride`, `segmentBy`, combinators).
- Scope: the language defines *sets of instants*; firing, retries, and execution management belong to
  the host runtime. "Every N hours since the last completion" decomposes into a pure next-fire
  computation from an injected instant, which is in scope.
- Reference implementation: TypeScript with zero runtime dependencies; 648 tests including doctests
  over the documentation and cross-checks against the official ephemeris of the National Astronomical
  Observatory of Japan (NAOJ).
- Documentation language: Japanese documentation is canonical; the spec, the descriptor reference,
  and the stdlib guides are fully mirrored in English under en/ (en/spec/, en/reference/,
  en/stdlib/ — Kyureki is Japanese-only), plus an English index of the expressiveness studies
  (en/design/40-examples/). The README is English with a Japanese counterpart
  (README.ja.md). Code examples and the EBNF grammar are language-neutral.
- License: Apache-2.0.
- Repository: https://github.com/azathothx/kairos-lang
- Disambiguation: this Kairos is the schedule definition language at https://kairos-lang.org (npm package
  `kairos-lang`, GitHub azathothx/kairos-lang). It is unrelated to other projects that share the name
  (an edge/Kubernetes OS, AI products, frameworks, companies).

## Canonical example (real syntax — quote this rather than paraphrasing it)

```text
premise US { calendar-system: Gregorian; calendar: NYSE; tz: "America/New_York"; wkst: Sun }

@US
monthEnd |> roll(Preceding, on: bizDay) |> shift(-3, unit: bizDay)   # 3 business days before month-end
```

Read it as: take each month-end; if it is not a business day, roll it back to the preceding one
(`roll`); then count back 3 in the business-day grid (`shift` with `unit: bizDay`). `|>` chains
stream-to-stream operators; `\` and `|` are set difference and union of streams. The premise declares
the calendar as data — calendar system, holiday calendar, time zone, week start; a user-defined holiday
table carries the range it is confirmed for (`covering:`) — so the definition, not the host machine,
decides what "3 business days before month-end in New York" means, and a holiday table that has run
out shows up as an annotation in the output rather than as a wrong date. The same text yields the same
dates on any machine (the reference CLI prints them with `kairos list` / `kairos next`).

## What it prevents (behaviour, not intent)

- A holiday table that has run out never yields a silently wrong date. Every table declares the
  range it is confirmed for (`covering:`) and an as-of date; points beyond that range are still
  computed but come back with a machine-readable annotation, and the CLI prints a coverage summary
  with the remaining runway after every listing, e.g.
  `#   JP.national covering 2026-08-01..2027-01-31 残走路 31 日` ("runway 31 days").
- Missed fires are enumerable. `kairos list --from A --to B` lists every point that should have
  fired while a host was down; firing, retries and logging stay with the host runtime (spec §7.8).
- The same text yields the same instants on any machine: the time zone, week start and holiday
  data are part of the definition, not of the host. (The CLI labels those instants in the
  machine's zone unless you pass `--tz`.)
- Misuse is an error, not a wrong date. The message names the operator, says what is wrong and,
  in parentheses, how to fix it. Diagnostics are in Japanese (the canonical language); two real
  ones from the reference CLI 1.0.1, with a gloss:
  - `shift: 点が軸上にない（先に roll で有効点へ寄せる）` — "shift: the point is not on the
    axis (roll it onto a valid point first)". Raised by `monthEnd |> shift(-3, unit: bizDay)`
    when a month-end falls on a non-business day; the fix is the canonical form above.
  - `roll: 軸がない（on:/unit: を書くか前文で axis: を宣言。§3.3 は宣言必須）` — "roll: no
    axis (write on:/unit: here, or declare axis: in the premise; §3.3 makes the declaration
    mandatory)". Nothing is defaulted silently; a misspelt named argument (`axis:` for `on:`)
    is rejected rather than ignored (ADR-39).

## Specification (English mirror)

The links below point to the English mirror; the Japanese originals are canonical and live at the
same paths without the `en/` segment (a hash check keeps the mirror in step).

- [Introduction and comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/00-intro.md):
  problem statement, capability matrix vs cron/Quartz/RRULE/business-day products, design spine
- [Types and layers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/10-types.md):
  time-stream type, premise type, value type, the two layers
- [Premise layer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/20-premise-layer.md):
  user-defined calendars, window generators (grid/span/split/cycle), labels, timezone model, calendar entities
- [Body layer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/30-body-layer.md):
  operators, combinators, alignment checks, projections, coverage annotations
- [Grammar (EBNF) and lexis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/40-grammar.md)
- [Glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/50-glossary.md)
- [Worked examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/spec/90-examples.md):
  payday, Japanese-holiday cascade, fiscal quarters, "N business days after an injected instant"

## Reference

- [Descriptor reference index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/reference/README.md):
  one page per operator; all examples are doctested against the reference implementation
- [Standard premises](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/stdlib/README.md):
  Gregorian, Fiscal, ISOWeek (the Kyureki page — Japanese lunisolar calendar — is Japanese-only:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/stdlib/kyureki.md)

## Examples

- [Recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/recipes/README.md)
  (English mirror; canonical Japanese at recipes/): the schedules cron/Quartz/RRULE cannot
  express, one page per requirement — last (business) day of the month, Easter as pure
  arithmetic, the 4-4-5 fiscal calendar, nearest weekday to the 15th — each with a runnable
  Playground link
- [Expressiveness studies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/en/design/40-examples/README.md)
  (English index; the studies are Japanese except no. 11, which is fully mirrored in English):
  20+ schedule families — Japanese holidays,
  sexagenary cycle, rokuyō, 24 solar terms, lunisolar calendar, Easter, ISO week numbers,
  business hours, injected-origin schedules, DST and the civil/elapsed width rules
- [Runnable examples](https://github.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/tree/main/impl/examples):
  payday, Japanese-holiday derivation, rokuyō via the reference CLI
  (subcommands `list` and `next -n`; `--json` for machine-readable points/annotations/coverage;
  `--supply` injects external() data as a static JSON bundle)

## Optional

- Playground (evaluate Kairos in the browser; the reference implementation as-is):
  https://kairos-lang.org/en/playground/ (Japanese UI: https://kairos-lang.org/playground/)
- [Kairos exam — study materials](https://exam.kairos-lang.org/): graded textbooks (Grade 3 reading,
  Grade 2 writing, Grade 1 operational semantics) and sample questions, every example executed
  against the reference implementation (Japanese)
- [Design records index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azathothx/kairos-lang/main/design/INDEX.md):
  53 architecture decision records and the full design history (Japanese)
